# Comparing Project and Delivery Leadership Courses

Choosing training for new team leads is harder than it looks. The market is full of courses that promise practical skills, recognised credentials and flexible schedules, and quality varies widely. We reviewed popular online programmes and spoke to learners and their managers about what actually made a difference.

## What learners valued

Learners consistently rated live interaction above polished video content. Courses with workshops or coaching calls had higher completion rates, and learners said they were more confident applying new skills at work afterwards.

FACT: Cohort-based courses in our review had a completion rate of 82 percent.
FACT: Self-paced courses had a completion rate of 47 percent.
FACT: Managers rated SkillForge 4 point 5 out of 5 for practical relevance.

## Credentials

Credentials matter more to some organisations than others. Learners early in their careers often valued a recognised certificate for their CV, while managers cared more about observable changes in behaviour. A course that includes an exam can provide both, provided it does not sacrifice practice for test preparation.

## Time commitment

Busy team leads often underestimate the time needed. Courses that ask for three to five hours per week fitted best alongside a full workload. Longer programmes were valuable but saw more learners fall behind during busy periods.

## Our advice

Match the course to the goal. For immediate day-to-day project skills, a short cohort course works well. For building a shared leadership vocabulary and a credential, a longer certified programme may be worth the extra time and cost.
